companies.name: Nudge
companies.funding_note: $100M Series A reported July 2025, led by Thrive Capital and Greenoaks. Secondary-source reporting only (The Debrief, Dealroom); headcount and some figures disagree across sources (32-50 employees). Verified 2026-10-17.
companies.security_notes: Non-invasive focused-ultrasound brain interface. First product 'Nudge Zero' in research use as of April 2026; no public security documentation found. Co-founded by Fred Ehrsam (Coinbase co-founder), Jeremy Barenholtz, Quintin Frerichs.

companies.name: Echo Neurotechnologies
companies.funding_note: ~$50M Series A reported January 2025, led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). Neither party publicly confirmed exact figures per press coverage. Verified 2026-10-17.
companies.security_notes: Implantable BCI company led by neurosurgeon Edward Chang (UCSF), targeting restoration of communication/movement for people with severe neurological disability. No public security documentation found. Development stage not independently confirmed (no peer-reviewed paper, regulatory filing, or trial report found).

companies.name: Epia Neuro
companies.headquarters: Alameda, California, USA (one source instead says San Francisco; unresolved)
companies.funding_note: No confirmed total. April 2026 public-debut coverage describes a mix of venture and pharmaceutical investment without a disclosed amount. Verified 2026-10-17.
companies.security_notes: Minimally invasive skull-implant 'read/write' BCI (non-dura-penetrating) for stroke-related upper-limb motor impairment, paired with an external grip-assist glove. Planned expansion to cognitive decline. Leadership: Michel Maharbiz PhD (CEO; also iota Biosciences co-founder), Gil Mandelbaum PhD (CTO/CSO), Michelle Patruno (COO). Planned first-in-human demonstrations at Lenox Hill Hospital, slated for 2026 (not yet completed as of this record). No public security documentation found.

companies.name: Kandu, Inc.
companies.funding_note: $30M first close co-led by Ally Bridge Group and AMED Ventures, announced with the April 2025 Kandu Health + Neurolutions merger (confirmed via Fierce Biotech, MedTech Dive, Healthcare Dive). CONFLICT: CB Insights lists total raised as $9.77M, and a Simplify.jobs listing claims an unconfirmed January 2026 round from K2 HealthVentures and Piper Sandler -- neither reconciled against a primary source; treat $30M as the best-supported figure and the others as unresolved. Verified 2026-10-17.
companies.security_notes: Formed by the April 2025 merger of Neurolutions, Inc. (device maker) and Kandu Health, Inc. (post-discharge stroke-recovery support service) under CEO Leo Petrossian. IpsiHand (Neurolutions) uses scalp EEG to detect ipsilateral motor intent and drive a hand/arm orthosis; received FDA De Novo clearance in 2021 -- company states this was the first BCI device to receive that clearance (company claim, not independently verified against the FDA database by this session). CMS created a procedure code and benefit-category determination for IpsiHand in 2024. A randomized controlled trial of IpsiHand (Dr. Eric Leuthardt) was reportedly presented at the International Stroke Conference 2026 (New Orleans, Feb 4-6, 2026) showing positive motor-gain results -- secondary-source reporting only, not independently confirmed against conference proceedings. No public device security documentation found. Prior to the merger, the two firms had partnered since 2023.

companies.name: Coherence Neuro
companies.funding_note: $10M seed round closed November 2025, co-led by Artesian and Topology Ventures (joined by Blackbird, Possible Ventures, and others). One secondary aggregator instead lists $13.46M total raised to date -- unresolved discrepancy, not independently reconciled. Verified 2026-10-17 via MassDevice and Seedtable.
companies.security_notes: Coin-sized wireless closed-loop brain implant paired with an over-ear wearable and companion app; records from and stimulates brain tissue, targeting glioblastoma by disrupting tumor bioelectric signaling. Designed to be placed during tumor-resection surgery. DEVICE-NAMING FLAG: called 'SOMA-1' in most profiles, but a June 2026 MassDevice report says the company began a first-in-human trial of an investigational device named 'Cipher' at Royal Melbourne Hospital (Australia), led by Dr. Andrew Morokoff -- the relationship between 'SOMA-1' and 'Cipher' is not resolved by available sources (same device renamed, or two different programs). Founded by Cambridge researchers Ben Woodington and Elise Jenkins; Neuralink head neurosurgeon Matthew MacDougall is an adviser/investor. No public security documentation found.

devices.name: SOMA-1 / Cipher (naming unresolved -- see security_notes)
devices.units_deployed: First-in-human trial reportedly begun June 2026 at Royal Melbourne Hospital, Australia (MassDevice); units deployed count not found

companies.name: iota Biosciences
companies.funding_note: This figure is acquisition deal consideration, NOT a funding round: Astellas Pharma's 2020 acquisition. Outlets disagree on the upfront-vs-milestone split (~$127.6M upfront + ~$176.5M milestones per UC Berkeley/Implantable Device reporting, vs. Fierce Biotech's headline framing of a $304M deal with $125M earmarked for program growth). Verified 2026-10-17 via BioSpace, Fierce Biotech, BusinessWire.
companies.security_notes: UC Berkeley-originated 'neural dust' technology: millimeter-scale, battery-free, ultrasound-powered wireless implants (Maharbiz/Carmena labs). Astellas and iota held a prior R&D agreement from August 2019 before the 2020 acquisition. No public security documentation found. Retained as an acquired/historical entry for M&A lineage (Astellas).

companies.name: BRILL Neurotech
companies.funding_note: No funding total found via independent sources beyond a listed Illinois state investment-fund recipient mention; not independently confirmed. Verified 2026-10-17.
companies.security_notes: GEOGRAPHY FLAG: headquartered in Urbana, Illinois, NOT California -- named in a 'Neurotech in California' newsletter post despite this; see gap-analysis.md. Non-invasive brain-imaging headset using Fast Optical Signals (FOS) to detect when and where neurons fire in real time; stated application areas include epilepsy diagnosis and improving BCI signal quality. Co-founded by Mehmet Gunal (Beckman Institute Cognitive Imaging Lab research affiliate). Filed a 'NEURODATA' USPTO trademark application (July 2025, covering brain-derived datasets; non-final office action as of filing). No public security documentation found.

adjacent_tech.name: Forecast Bio
adjacent_tech.note: NOT a BCI or device company -- an AI/computational biology platform linking cellular neurobiology to mental-health drug effects. Included for sensor/data convergence relevance to neurosecurity (brain-circuit modeling data could itself be a sensitive data-security surface). San Francisco, California; March 2026 accelerator round reported (amount not found). Verified 2026-10-17 via One Mind and Dealroom profiles.
adjacent_tech.relevance: Preclinical AI platform modeling drug effects on brain circuits for mental-health therapeutics; relevant to QIF NeuroAI/software threat surface even though it builds no hardware device.
